intent: The first that happened in the 'wrong' place: a counter of the thirty people in the theatre, a pin on the hospital, then three survival silhouettes — 18 days, 19 months, 12 years — that turn a night in 1967 into a routine operation.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country saw the FIRST human heart transplant?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country saw the first human heart transplant?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat
lines.text: United States, South Africa, or United Kingdom?
Cape Town. On 3 December 1967 a surgeon called Christiaan Barnard gave a grocer a new heart.

lines.direction: tighten on the Cape; a crossed-out US sticker on 'American'; the US flag-ball thinks and the STANFORD card lands on 'Stanford'; the hospital tag, a team sticker and the counter running 0 → 30 on 'team'; a moon on 'overnight' as South Africa pulses
lines.text: Not an American first. Stanford had rehearsed for years; a South African team of 30 beat them, overnight.

lines.direction: ease back over the country; three survival silhouettes rise on 'days' — 18 days a sliver, 19 months a stub, 12 years a tower; a calendar sticker on 'months'; a heart sticker on 'years' as South Africa pulses
lines.text: The patient lived 18 days. The next lived 19 months. Today half of recipients pass 12 years.

lines.direction: tighten on Cape Town; the THE DONOR card on 'donor'; a candle sticker; the South African flag-ball, quiet, on 'father'; South Africa pulses softly on 'night'; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: The donor was a young woman killed crossing the road. Her father agreed that night.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A grocer, a surgeon, 18 days. Follow us.
